reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, selected R4/R6 package StructureDefinitions, direct endpoint/search behavior findings, and shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. The deterministic aggregate was used only after forming the resource-level judgment. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was treated as context because the reviewed artifact is neither Resource nor DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 FMM 0/trial-use materially lowers the compatibility burden for preserving the old resource identity and exact wire shape. It does not erase safety and regulatory relevance: contraindication applicability, related therapy, indication linkage, and population qualifiers can affect patient-safety or regulated product-information workflows.

overall.oneLineConclusion: MedicinalProductContraindication must migrate to ClinicalUseDefinition, but several low-cost or safety-relevant preservation questions still deserve standards attention.

reasoning.thesisMd: R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication` is not a same-name R6 resource; its successor is `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type = contraindication` and contraindication-specific content in a branch. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before old R4 instances, endpoints, searches, generated models, and references can work in R6. However, migration unavoidability is not the same as saying additional breaks are irrelevant: the reviewed findings include avoidable or expert-dependent changes around indication references, related therapy names, and population modeling.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration is a resource replacement and model consolidation, not a simple element rename. R4 resource identity becomes `ClinicalUseDefinition`; a required `type` discriminator selects the contraindication branch; top-level contraindication details move under `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`; `subject` becomes mandatory and changes to `CodeableReference`; condition fields use `CodeableReference`; `therapeuticIndication` changes from a reference to inline indication content; `otherTherapy` reuses a differently named backbone; and inline `Population` changes to `Reference(Group)`. The direct behavior reports reinforce this shape because the old REST endpoint advertisement and old resource-specific search surface disappear.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The removed resource identity sharply lowers the leverage of preserving every old element path: a raw R4 payload still needs an explicit transform and endpoint/search migration. The right posture is therefore not pure per-change preservation. But low-cost compatibility still has value where it reduces lossy or expert-dependent migration after the resource transform, especially preserving indication link semantics, accepting or aliasing old `otherTherapy` child names, and providing an inline-population transition path or clear Group-creation rules.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Less-breaking designs are weak for the top-level resource identity, the required `type` discriminator, and the mandatory `subject` requirement because they are central to the merged ClinicalUseDefinition model and safety/computability. They are more plausible for `therapeuticIndication` (allow inline content or a reference to an indication ClinicalUseDefinition), `otherTherapy` (retain/deprecate old child names or accept aliases while broadening semantics), and `population` (allow `population[x]` or retain inline Population alongside Group references). Non-required local terminology bindings are already compatibility-preserving enough at the base level.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The in-scope behavior findings are derivative but important: the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises the old resource endpoint, and search parameters whose only R4 base was MedicinalProductContraindication disappear with the endpoint. These do not add a separate rationale for every element change, but they confirm that implementers need endpoint, route, search, and conformance-metadata migration guidance, not only instance transforms. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation/search findings are contextual only for this resource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is unavoidable and that the migration shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`. I only partially agree with its `migration-program-dominates` compatibility posture. That label is defensible for the resource identity break, but the holistic review gives more weight to the three Revisit findings where preservation or transition support could still reduce safety-relevant or expert-dependent migration costs.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural and behavior mechanics from the local R4/R6 packages and reports. The main uncertainty is production prevalence and official design rationale: the local evidence does not prove broad use of this exact FMM 0 R4 resource, nor does it include authoritative migration notes for all IDMP successor mappings.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 MedicinalProductContraindication resource is removed and replaced by ClinicalUseDefinition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the core reason a resource-level migration program is unavoidable. Same-name R6 validation, generated classes, references, and REST routes cannot preserve R4 instances without transforming resource identity. Because the artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, a parallel deprecated base resource is not clearly low-cost enough to demand.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 requires a type discriminator and contraindication branch consistency
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The required `type = contraindication` value is a hard validation requirement after transformation, but it is deterministic for every migrated R4 contraindication and is central to the merged resource. It is mainly a required migration rule, not an avoidable resource-level concern.

findingConsiderations.title: Subject becomes mandatory and changes from Reference to CodeableReference with different targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Missing-subject R4 instances need remediation and present references need wrapping and target migration. This is central to the meaning of a contraindication and has a plausible safety rationale, so it is not the strongest preservation candidate despite being a material migration chore.

findingConsiderations.title: Top-level contraindication details move under ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication with renamed paths
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The branch move expresses the ClinicalUseDefinition consolidation. Keeping old top-level fields in the base model would duplicate facts and conflict with branch/type consistency, so this mostly belongs to the accepted resource redesign rather than a low-cost local fix.

findingConsiderations.title: therapeuticIndication Reference is replaced by inline contraindication.indication content
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This remains important even after accepting the broader migration. Replacing an independent reference with inline content can require dereferencing, preserving identifiers/provenance, handling missing or reused indications, and making expert mapping choices. A reference-preserving option to an indication ClinicalUseDefinition looks worth standards review.

findingConsiderations.title: otherTherapy child names and medication representation change
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The CodeableReference and target updates have an R6 modeling rationale, but renaming `therapyRelationshipType` and `medication[x]` to `relationshipType` and `treatment` appears more avoidable. Deprecated aliases or retaining old child names could reduce wire-format and codegen churn at modest cost.

findingConsiderations.title: population changes from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Population criteria often determine whether a contraindication applies. Migrating inline age, gender, race, or physiological-condition criteria to Group references can require creating external resources, preserving traceability, and deciding whether down-conversion is possible. A `population[x]` or inline transitional shape deserves review despite FMM 0.

findingConsiderations.title: Disease, diseaseStatus, and comorbidity change from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real wire-shape change, but the R4-to-R6 mapping is usually mechanical by placing the old CodeableConcept under `.concept`. Reverse conversion can be lossy when R6 uses `.reference`, yet the uniform CodeableReference pattern is proportionate in the successor model.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds modifier status with no R4 counterpart
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new optional modifier status is safety-relevant for R6-to-R4 down-conversion, but it does not block R4-to-R6 migration. The right mitigation is explicit down-conversion loss handling or extension policy rather than removing the R6 element.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 introduces local terminology bindings where R4 had none
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The local bindings are example or preferred, not required, so base R6 validation remains permissive for old codes. This may affect UI or profile choices but is not a material base compatibility break.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Because MedicinalProductContraindication is among the removed endpoints, clients that discover or generate routes from the base CapabilityStatement need a route-level migration. This is derivative of resource replacement but confirms that the break is not only an instance-validation issue.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Old MedicinalProductContraindication searches cannot be run unchanged once the endpoint is gone. Search migration should be specified together with the ClinicalUseDefinition successor mapping, but the finding does not independently justify or reject each structural redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This and the other shared Resource/DomainResource operation/search findings may affect generic clients, but they are not specific to MedicinalProductContraindication and were not scored as resource-level compatibility pressure.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish an authoritative migration map from R4 `MedicinalProductContraindication` to R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition`, including `resourceType` replacement, `type = contraindication`, branch moves, subject wrapping/target migration, population handling, and endpoint/search replacements.

Revisit low-cost transition support for `therapeuticIndication`, `otherTherapy`, and `population`, because these changes can be lossy, expert-dependent, or avoidable beyond the unavoidable resource identity migration.

Document route and search migration expectations for former `MedicinalProductContraindication` clients, including whether servers should expose legacy aliases, redirects, compatibility profiles, or only explicit out-of-band transforms.

Define an R6-to-R4 loss policy for R6-only `status`, `identifier`, `category`, `management`, `applicability`, and `library` content so safety or lifecycle information is not silently discarded in mixed-version environments.

caveats: The review relies on local R4/R6 package evidence and generated reports; no authoritative HL7 migration narrative was available in the supplied inputs.
R4 FMM 0/trial-use means the review does not assume broad production dependence, even though the domain is safety and regulatory relevant.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context, consistent with the review contract.
